blockers.title: Golden gate's engine leg is structurally dead: nothing ever writes docs/goldens/.engine-probe.json, so the engine-vs-standalone cross-runner compare never runs; --bless (the golden's documented engine-side producer) requires the engine and has never executed
blockers.evidence: compare-golden.sh: `if [ -f docs/goldens/.engine-probe.json ]; then` — repo-wide grep for 'engine-probe' finds only these two consumer lines, no producer. --bless path: `if [ "$ENGINE_PRESENT" -eq 0 ]; then echo "cannot --bless without the engine"`. Verifier mechanically confirmed the committed golden's values match the standalone runner byte-for-byte (honest standalone-sourced pin), but the engine PPProbe output can never reach the comparison.
blockers.detail: The ODN-11 cross-runner contract (engine PPProbe ≡ standalone spine-check ≡ golden) is enforced on two of three legs only; the engine leg is unreachable dead code forever, not just at this sha.
blockers.recommended_fix: In run-tests-headless.sh --probe, write the JSON to docs/goldens/.engine-probe.json (or have local-ci.sh pass --json-out there in gate 6) so gate 7's engine branch becomes reachable; document that --bless re-records the committed golden.

blockers.title: Format gate is false-green: labeled ENGINE: so it skips at this sha although format-check.sh is engine-free (system clang-format fallback), and 8/16 Source files FAIL clang-format when actually run — README/AGENTS/PR all claim the pre-engine 'format, spine, static' loop is green
blockers.evidence: GATES[0] = "ENGINE:Format (clang-format --dry-run on Source/)|scripts/format-check.sh" → SKIP when ENGINE_PRESENT=0. Verifier ran format-check.sh directly: exit 1 with exactly 8 NOT FORMATTED files (PP_Hash.h, PP_Rng.h, PP_Sim.h, PP_DeterminismTests.cpp, PP_HashTests.cpp, PP_RngTests.cpp, PPProbeCommandlet.cpp, PPProbeCommandlet.h). Homebrew clang-format 22.1.8 present on this machine. README: 'format / spine / static gates run without the engine'; local-ci.sh --fast help: 'gates 1-3 only (the pre-engine loop: format, spine, static)'. Spine headers use one-line braced returns conflicting with the committed Allman .clang-format.
blockers.detail: The briefing's requirement 'engine-free gates must be green at this sha' is false for format: the gate silently skips and would fail — the exact false-green class AGENTS.md's own pitfalls forbid.
blockers.recommended_fix: Drop the ENGINE: prefix from gate 1 (the script self-skips gracefully when no clang-format exists) and run clang-format -i over the 8 files; verify --fast goes green.

blockers.title: PPProbe commandlet cannot compile: ParseCommandLine is called with 2 args but UE has only the 3-arg (Tokens, Switches) overload — and even arity-fixed, -seed/-ticks/-json tokens route to Switches, never Tokens
blockers.evidence: `TArray<FString> Tokens; ParseCommandLine(*Params, Tokens);` — the engine's global ParseCommandLine(const TCHAR*, TArray<FString>&, TArray<FString>&) is the only overload; dash-prefixed args are classified as switches (dash-stripped), so the loop `for (const FString& Token : Tokens)` would never see -seed=42/-ticks=100/-json=… and the commandlet would always run defaults.
blockers.detail: The headless probe entry — a lens-guard requirement of the spine port — is non-runnable as shipped; it fails at compile time, and the parse is wrong even if it compiled.
blockers.recommended_fix: Use the 3-arg overload, iterate Switches (or UCommandlet's parsed members), match with StartsWith("seed=") after the dash strip; test with the engine once installed.

blockers.title: PPProbeCommandlet.cpp uses LogPPCore without including the header that declares it (PacketPlumberCore.h)
blockers.evidence: UE_LOG(LogPPCore, …) used three times; LogPPCore is declared only via `DECLARE_LOG_CATEGORY_EXTERN(LogPPCore, Log, All)` in Source/PacketPlumberCore/PacketPlumberCore.h, which is not in the .cpp's include list (nor in PPProbeCommandlet.h).
blockers.detail: Second independent compile breaker in the commandlet: undeclared identifier at the first UE_LOG.
blockers.recommended_fix: #include "PacketPlumberCore/PacketPlumberCore.h" (after B5's include-path fix) or move the category into a header both modules share.

blockers.title: Module-prefixed spine includes cannot resolve: headers sit flat in Source/PacketPlumberCore/ (no Public/), no Build.cs adds explicit include paths, yet tests/editor include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_*.h" — under BuildSettingsVersion.V5 the PacketPlumberCoreTests and PacketPlumberEditor modules cannot compile
blockers.evidence: All cross-module includes are module-prefixed (e.g. #include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Rng.h") while the headers live at the module root with no Public/ folder; PacketPlumberCore.Build.cs declares only PCHUsage + PublicDependencyModuleNames — no PublicIncludePaths/PrivateIncludePaths; both .Target.cs pin DefaultBuildSettings = BuildSettingsVersion.V5. Default V5 include rules put the module dir itself on dependents' paths (resolving "PP_Rng.h"), never the Source/ parent needed for the prefixed form.
blockers.detail: Every engine-side translation unit that touches the spine fails include resolution — the UE automation suite and commandlet cannot build when the engine lands.
blockers.recommended_fix: Either move spine headers to Source/PacketPlumberCore/Public/PacketPlumberCore/ (matching the prefixed includes) or add PublicIncludePaths.Add(Path.Combine(ModuleDirectory, "../")) — the standard UE5 layout is the safer fix.

blockers.title: Magic-byte assertion is reversed: FPPStateSerializeVersioned asserts bytes 'P','P','U','E' but the LE serializer emits 'E','U','P','P' for SAVE_MAGIC 0x50505545 — the determinism suite fails at engine time
blockers.evidence: SAVE_MAGIC = 0x50505545u; PutU32 writes LSB-first → Buffer[0]=0x45 'E', [1]=0x55 'U', [2]=0x50 'P', [3]=0x50 'P'. Test: TestEqual("magic byte 0", Buffer[0], uint8_t('P')) … 'P','P','U','E'. Exactly one side of the wire contract is wrong.
blockers.detail: A committed spine test asserting the opposite of the serializer guarantees the PacketPlumber.* suite reports failure the moment the engine builds — the cross-runner contract would false-fail.
blockers.recommended_fix: Pick one truth: either assert Buffer = 'E','U','P','P' (LE of the constant as written) or change SAVE_MAGIC so LE bytes spell P,P,U,E; document the chosen wire format.

warnings.evidence: grep for bTerminal/backward across tests/ + PacketPlumberCoreTests/ (excluding PP_Sim.h) returns nothing; both suites only step forward 1..100.

warnings.title: run-tests-headless.sh --probe prints "probe JSON written" without asserting the artifact exists; the RESULT=OK log-grep can pass even when the JSON write failed
warnings.evidence: The commandlet logs RESULT=OK before the JSON write; on write failure it returns 1 after the OK line is already in the log. The script greps for RESULT=OK then echoes 'probe JSON written to …' unconditionally — no [ -f ] check.
warnings.detail: The golden gate could consume a stale/missing engine JSON — success must be asserted on artifacts, per the repo's own pitfall notes.
warnings.recommended_fix: After the run: [ -s "$JSON_OUT" ] || { echo 'probe JSON missing'; exit 1; }

warnings.title: FNV-1a conformance is partially tautological: Fnv1a64(x) == Fnv1a64(x) pins nothing; the only real vector is the empty-input offset basis
warnings.evidence: `CHECK(PP::Fnv1a64(PP, 2) == PP::Fnv1a64(PP, 2), "fnv1a64(pp) must be deterministic")` — a pure function compared to itself. The empty-input == FNV64_OFFSET check IS a real vector; nothing else is.
warnings.detail: A broken FNV implementation that returns a constant nonzero hash passes every current hash test except the empty/offset one.
warnings.recommended_fix: Pin published FNV-1a-64 vectors (e.g. Fnv1a64("a") = 0xaf63dc4c8601ec8c, Fnv1a64("foobar") = 0x85944171f73967e8) in both runners.

warnings.title: .mcp.json runs an unpinned third-party npm package with agent privileges: npx -y ue-mcp resolves latest on every boot
warnings.evidence: "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ue-mcp", "PacketPlumberUE.uproject"] — no version pin, -y auto-installs, and the server drives the editor with write access.
warnings.detail: A moved/compromised latest tag silently becomes the agent's editor driver on next boot — non-reproducible agent tooling.
warnings.recommended_fix: Pin the package (npx -y ue-mcp@<version> …) and record the pinned version + upgrade step in docs/agent-playbook.md.
